persona.name: Nadezhda
persona.bio:
Живу в Барселоне, пишу код, ухаживаю за зелеными
А завтра посмотрим
persona.archetype: thoughtful nomad who settled — finds meaning in routines, friends, and small sensory moments rather than achievements

language.secondary: English (~11% — always short, often witty or poetic)
language.mixing_pattern: Russian for reflection and storytelling; English for dry one-liners, location labels, and cultural references
language.script_notes: uses 'digital номадства', 'girls-only trip' — casual code-switching mid-sentence in Russian text

voice_dimensions.intimacy: writes as if to close friends, not a public audience — confessional, warm, presupposing shared context
voice_dimensions.self_irony: undercuts sentimentality with deadpan humor; never takes herself too seriously
voice_dimensions.sensory_precision: anchors memories in specific details: smell of fresh bread, thin floral porcelain cups, the sound of jazz
voice_dimensions.anti_hustle: explicitly values repetition and routine over achievement lists; resists productivity culture framing
voice_dimensions.emotional_honesty: names anxiety, doubt, and longing directly without dramatizing them
voice_dimensions.cultural_fluency: drops Gilmore Girls, Midnight in Paris, Into the Wild references naturally, no explanation

short_phrase.description: single evocative sentence or phrase, often a standalone image caption
examples_ru: Все поняли, что я люблю Берлин?
El fin de semana en Cataluña
examples_en: Your mom in Barcelona in her twenties
If I seem lost in my thoughts, just know that mentally I'm there

place_date_label.description: minimal caption: title/mood word + place + date, no commentary

personal_reflection.description: lyrical, diary-style storytelling — specific memories, lists of sensory details, honest emotional accounting
structural_features: often opens with a setting or provocation, not a thesis
uses enumeration to build emotional cumulation (series of small moments)
ends on quiet landing, not a punchline
no hashtags in recent long captions
examples_excerpt: Несколько лет кружочков в телеграмме, реедких встреч в Москве и обещания «когда-нибудь»… И вдруг мы и самом деле в поезде…
В этом году я не переехала, не выучила новый язык, не пробежала марафон… радуюсь другим повторяющимся цифрам: 4 дня в неделю хожу в офис (добровольно!)
Пока новый год потихоньку набирает свои обороты, вспоминаю самый «барселонский» момент прошлого — рассветная прогулка по безлюдному пляжу однажды в пятницу перед работой

what_she_never_does: hashtag spam or keyword stuffing (zero hashtags in posts from 2024–2026)
calls to action (no 'link in bio', no 'drop a comment', no 'save this post')
achievement brag framing ('I did X, Y, Z this year')
exclamation marks in earnest (used sparingly and self-aware)
perfect-life aesthetics or curated positivity without shadow

sensory_anchors: coffee (specific: thin porcelain, cappuccino, morning ritual)
emotional_themes: the texture of friendship and physical closeness
the pleasure of settling into routine
the gap between fantasy and real life (always affectionate, not bitter)
cultural_references: Gilmore Girls ('Hold on tight, spider monkey')

travel_footprint.travel_style: arrives as a wanderer, leaves as a regular — seeks cafés, walks, locals, not landmarks

punctuation_and_style_fingerprints.em_dash: primary rhythm device — used where comma or period could go
punctuation_and_style_fingerprints.ellipsis: rare but meaningful; signals trailing thought, not incompletion
punctuation_and_style_fingerprints.sentence_length: alternates between very short fragments and long rolling sentences in the same caption
punctuation_and_style_fingerprints.lowercase_english: sometimes used for vulnerability or quieter register: 'there's been a month me missing home', 'i'm just a simple russian girl'
punctuation_and_style_fingerprints.no_hashtags: in all posts from approximately 2024 onwards

ideal_post_formula.short: one image, one phrase — captures the mood without explaining it
ideal_post_formula.medium: image + place + month/year — minimal but anchored
ideal_post_formula.long: opens in the middle of a moment → expands into memory or feeling via list of sensory details → closes quietly, no moral or lesson

do: anchor to a specific place, time, and sensory detail
let the mood sit without explaining it
mix mundane and meaningful without hierarchy
be self-aware about clichés — name them before using them ('Cliché, but...')
celebrate small repeated rituals as the substance of a good life
switch to English for dry wit or cultural reference one-liners
dont: summarize what happened ('We had such an amazing time!')
name-drop places as status ('Was in Paris this week!')
